LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 3.3.1. OBJECTIVE PRONOUNS • SINGULAR • PLURAL

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.3: Language Use 3.3.1. Objective pronouns • Singular • Plural
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language Use 3.3.1. Objective pronouns • Singular • Plural, part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How do we talk about a person without mentioning their name?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to a story/poem/conversation featuring objective pronouns (me, us, you, him/her, them).

2. pick out singular and plural objective plurals in the text.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to a story/poem/conversation featuring objective pronouns (me, us, you, him/her, them).
2. pick out singular and plural objective plurals in the text.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language Use 3.3.1. Objective pronouns • Singular • Plural together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration; as the learner’s ability to listen keenly and actively is enhanced as they listen attentively to recognise the singular

and plural objective pronouns.

Values:
Unity; the learner’s ability to cooperate is enhanced as they work collaboratively with others in group discussions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: the learner’s self-esteem and nurtured as they are able to construct sentences using objective pronouns.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Objective pronouns are learnt in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.
